evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/meters/components/ReadingForm.tsx:107-116 — when `enableOcr` is set and the user attaches a meter photo, the form calls `await processOcr(file)` inside a try/catch whose catch body is ONLY `console.error('OCR processing failed')` (line 115) with no user-facing feedback. On OCR failure the component sets none of its OCR state (setOcrResult / setOcrImageUrl / setShowOcrPreview are skipped), so the OCR preview panel simply never appears and `showOcrPreview` stays false. The user who opted into OCR gets zero signal that it ran and failed — they are left staring at a form that silently did nothing, with the only trace in the browser console.

The inline comment `// OCR failed, user can still enter value manually` documents the intended graceful-degradation behavior, but the degradation is not communicated: there is no toast, no inline hint ('OCR unavailable, enter the reading manually'), and no i18n key for the failure. Every other error surface in this segment (settings/notifications/advanced errors.*, emergency/errors.failedTo*, documents/folder.loadError) uses a user-visible i18n'd message; this OCR path is the outlier.

Landable frontend-only remedy: set a small non-blocking OCR-status state in the catch (e.g. setOcrError(t('meters.reading.ocrFailed'))) and render it near the photo field, with a new i18n key under meters.reading. Severity low: the form remains fully usable via manual entry and no data is lost or corrupted; the gap is purely a missing user-feedback/i18n affordance on an optional convenience path. Confidence medium: statically confirmed the catch body logs only and leaves OCR preview state untouched; not runtime-executed.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/pages/ContentModerationPage.tsx:205-208 — handleViewContent navigates to an internal SPA route via a full page reload: `window.location.href = `/compliance/moderation/cases/${caseId}``. ppt-web is a react-router-dom SPA; assigning window.location.href for an in-app route forces a full document reload, re-downloads the JS bundle, tears down all TanStack Query cache and React state, and drops the moderation list scroll/filter position. The code self-documents the shortcut: `// TODO(Phase-2): Use React Router's useNavigate for SPA navigation` / `// Phase 1: Full page reload for simplicity`.

Same window.location.href-for-SPA-route anti-pattern already flagged for RegistryPage.tsx (code-review-ppt-web-ui-registry-full-reload-nav, 2026-11-01). This is a DISTINCT file/handler not previously surfaced; emitted separately so it is independently landable. The compliance moderation queue is a manager-facing list where full-reload-on-view is a more noticeable regression than usual (reviewers click through many cases in sequence).

Landable frontend-only remedy: replace with react-router's useNavigate — `const navigate = useNavigate(); ... navigate(`/compliance/moderation/cases/${caseId}`)` — matching the convention used across the other 14 route groups. Severity low: navigation still functions, only the UX/perf degrades (lost SPA state, full reload). Confidence medium: statically confirmed the assignment targets an internal route and the file does not import useNavigate; not runtime-executed.
